author: Subhranil Mukherjee
headline: Senior Data Analyst | Financial Data Analysis | SQL | Power BI | Advanced Excel | KPI Dashboards | Retail & Operations Analytics | Ex-Amazonian | Ex- Target
text:
🚀 Recently appeared for a Deloitte interview for an Analyst role — and here are some of the questions I was asked 👇

If you're preparing for Data Analyst / BI roles, this might help you:

🔹 SQL
• Difference between LEFT JOIN and INNER JOIN
• CROSS JOIN — use cases and risks
• Find total salary by department
• Count of employees in each department
• Cumulative revenue over time (with and without window functions)
• Self Join — find employee and manager name

🔹 Power BI / DAX
• SAMEPERIODLASTYEAR() — how it works
• Bookmarks — use cases and implementation
• Cardinality — impact on data modeling
• RLS (Row Level Security) — static vs dynamic
• Writing measures like Total Sales, YoY %

🔹 Concepts & Scenarios
• When to use SUM vs SUMX
• Handling NULLs in aggregations
• Difference between COUNT, COUNTROWS, DISTINCTCOUNT
• Star schema vs flat table
• Performance considerations in Power BI

💡 One thing I realized:
Interviews are less about memorizing syntax and more about understanding why and when to use concepts.

If you're preparing — focus on fundamentals + real-world scenarios.

Happy to help anyone preparing for similar roles. Let’s grow together 🙌

text:
You spent years mastering SQL.

Now every job posting wants PySpark. 😬

Most engineers think:
"I need to learn a completely new language."

𝐇𝐞𝐫𝐞'𝐬 𝐰𝐡𝐚𝐭 𝐧𝐨𝐛𝐨𝐝𝐲 𝐭𝐞𝐥𝐥𝐬 𝐲𝐨𝐮:

PySpark isn't just "SQL for big data"
PySpark is SQL with Software Engineering superpowers. ⚡

𝐖𝐡𝐲 𝐏𝐲𝐒𝐩𝐚𝐫𝐤 > Raw 𝐒𝐐𝐋:

✅ Chainable methods (no nested hell)
✅ Type safety (catches errors early)
✅ Test locally (no database needed)
✅ Distributed automatically (built for scale)

𝐓𝐡𝐞 𝐛𝐫𝐮𝐭𝐚𝐥 𝐭𝐫𝐮𝐭𝐡:

SQL is great for Analytic Queries.
PySpark is built for Data Pipelines.

SQL is "What" you want.
PySpark gives you control over "How" it’s processed.

Here are some areas candidates were tested on:

✓ Handling Slowly Changing Dimensions. SCD Type 2. 🧩

✓ SQL tricks to remove duplicates and find the second highest salary. 🔍

✓ Designing daily incremental data pipelines. ⚙️

✓ Optimizing slow SQL queries and handling large datasets. ⚡

✓ Understanding INNER JOIN vs LEFT JOIN and OLTP vs OLAP. 🔗

✓ Working with Data Lakes, Azure Data Lake layers, and Python for data cleaning. 🗂️🐍

✓ Performing incremental loads in Azure Data Factory and handling inconsistent source data. 🔄

Data engineering interviews now focus on real world problem solving. 🧠

Not just writing basic SQL queries.

If you are preparing for interviews, focus on concepts, pipelines, and performance thinking. 🎯
